best_narrative.headline: Zocdoc: Telehealth Rivals Escalate Federal Lobbying on Prescription Economics
best_narrative.body: Zocdoc operates a healthcare provider directory and appointment marketplace with embedded telehealth provider listings, creating material exposure to state medical advertising regulations and fee-splitting statutes that govern how telehealth operators monetize provider relationships. Four competing telehealth platforms filed federal lobbying disclosures on prescription economics and telehealth access between March and May 2026, signaling coordinated industry mobilization around reimbursement policy and provider compensation models. Industry-standard regulatory exposures for directory-marketplace operators in this segment include anti-kickback statute compliance, consumer protection claim substantiation, and state-specific medical advertising approval workflows. New York's medical board and consumer protection bureau maintain active enforcement postures on telehealth advertising and provider fee arrangements, creating operational chokepoints for multistate directory platforms.

Would a 15-minute call on Thursday work to map exposure across your top three states? Best,
[Rep Name]

Two competitors in the mental health telehealth segment filed federal lobbying disclosures on telehealth policy as of April 2026, signaling intensified advocacy around reimbursement, licensure portability, and regulatory scope. Industry-standard regulatory exposures for this business model include state-by-state behavioral health board authority over prescribing and supervision standards, particularly in New York, California, and Florida. The competitor mobilization pattern suggests policy inflection points that may require proactive government affairs positioning before state legislatures move on mental health telehealth scope-of-practice or reimbursement guardrails.
